correctness.rationale: The boolean-update proof is coherent: with hub 0, rim y_i=x_(i−1)x_(i+1); with hub 1, rim updates by neighbor OR; two-step return with switching hub requires 2m>n, 2e<n and each occupied rim site has at least one distance-two occupied neighbor. For constant-hub returns, the step-two graph has one component for odd n and two for even n, giving exactly two monochromatic fixed states plus two constant-hub two-cycle orbits when n even. Cyclic words with no isolated ones are enumerated by Q_L(u,v) using run-length compositions, and their coefficient restriction gives B_n and T_n for all n≥3. Independently enumerated every configuration with n=3..11 and matched fixed counts and two-cycle populations, with equality boundary ties treated exactly; infinite proof is combinatorial and does not rest on those checks.

The present theorem only gives a sparse-subsequence exponential bound B_(6t+3)≥2^t and no new global count.

There is no uncovered small n or novel global orbit classification in the current record.
